matchup_findings.statement: Auburn's explosive rushing offense meets a Ole Miss defense that allows explosive rush plays (+2.47).

Auburn owns the stronger opponent-adjusted explosive-play matchup: Ole Miss offense vs Auburn defense -0.28, Auburn offense vs Ole Miss defense +1.21 (explosive-play rate, opponent-adjusted: Auburn offense #23 of 138, Ole Miss defense #87 of 138).

Ole Miss owns the stronger opponent-adjusted sustained-efficiency matchup: Ole Miss offense vs Auburn defense +1.29, Auburn offense vs Ole Miss defense -0.41 (success rate, opponent-adjusted: Ole Miss offense #8 of 138, Auburn defense #64 of 138).
Both offenses and both defenses point to more snaps than an average FBS game (possession environment +1.80).
Ole Miss's sustained-efficiency edge is real but not decisive (1.70, below the 2.0 strong threshold): enough for the trailing side to stay in range.
Ole Miss's offense has given the ball away at a high rate (+1.10 SD). Regression-prone: reported as volatility, never as a cause on its own.

pace.definition: possession_environment = (z of home offense plays + z of away defense plays allowed + z of away offense plays + z of home defense plays allowed) / 2, on adjusted values. Positive = more snaps than an average FBS game. tempo_environment = -(z of each offense's possession seconds per play) / 2

volatility.definition: offense_ypp_residual_sd = game-to-game spread of the offense's yards per play around what the fit expected against each opponent; its percentile is within the FBS universe. explosive_yard_share_z is the raw share standardised across FBS (not opponent-adjusted). takeaways_per_game_z and giveaways_per_game_z are RAW per-game turnover counts standardised across FBS: turnovers are regression-prone and are deliberately not opponent-adjusted.
